newsitem.title: GERMANY: Low EU sun oil prices may boost exports - Oil World.
newsitem.headline: Low EU sun oil prices may boost exports - Oil World.

text.p: Active sunflowerseed crushings in the European Union since June had weighed down oil prices and could encourage third country exports, Oil World newsletter said.
Higher sunflower seed imports from Russia, Ukraine and South Africa lifted EU crushings in the third quarter of 1996 by 16 percent to 928,000 tonnes and seed imports would continue.
EU sunflowerseed processing also picked up as a result of high rapeseed prices and tight supplies due to lower domestic crops.
EU sunflower oil prices had lost their premium versus Argentine origin and this could boost export chances on a cif basis in North Africa and elsewhere, Oil World said.
Oil World quoted fob November Argentine sun oil at $510 a tonne on Oct 24 (up two percent on the week) when its sun oil price at north west European ports was $515 (down 3.7 percent).
Oil World said the European price average in September was $588 and Argentina's $547.

It added Russia and Ukraine were exporting sunflowerseed from lower domestic crops under financial pressure. This may depress their domestic crushings and raise imports of other seeds, oils, fats and meals.
